Lauraceae.key_door: aromatic woody plant + no stipules + tiny trimerous flowers + valvate anthers + superior one-ovule ovary → one-seeded fleshy fruit/cupule

Magnoliaceae.key_door: annular stipule scar + large terminal flower with numerous tepals/stamens/pistils + elongate receptacle → cone-like follicetum + red arillate seeds

Saururaceae.key_door: rhizomatous wetland herb + stipular petiole sheath + long raceme of perianthless flowers + schizocarp

taxonomy_notes: Camphora officinarum, Lindera benzoin, Magnolia grandiflora, and Saururus cernuus are accepted current concepts.
Cinnamomum camphora is retained as synonym provenance for accepted Camphora officinarum.
Camphora officinarum is introduced in Texas; Lindera benzoin, Magnolia grandiflora, and Saururus cernuus have Texas in current native-range treatments.
Joey Santore saved-media routing was checked first; no direct target-family frame is currently indexed for these three families.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not treat aroma alone as sufficient for Lauraceae.
Do not teach Magnolia from flower size alone; preserve stipule-scar and aggregate-fruit architecture.
Do not mistake the entire Saururus raceme for one flower; each tiny flower lacks a perianth.
